articles.title: Ice Hockey Association of India faction moves the Delhi HC against declaration of Usha’s nomination - Sportstar
articles.summary: Ice Hockey Association of India faction moves the Delhi HC against declaration of Usha’s nomination Sportstar
articles.content: New Delhi A faction of the Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI) has moved the Delhi High Court, seeking to declare the inclusion of Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha in the electoral rolls for the December 5 elections as “void and unlawful”. The Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI), led by Gurpreet Singh Bakshi, had nominated Usha as one of its representatives to the IOA General Assembly after she lost the Sportspersons of Merit (SOMs) election. The other member nominated was its secretary-general, Harjinder Singh. Another faction led by Kunzang Namgyal objected to the nomination of Usha, contending that she was never a member of the Ice Hockey Association of India. It also claimed that Bakshi and Harjinder have no authority to function as president and secretary general of the IHAI, “as they do not have any legal mandate to hold these offices”. The IOA recognises Ice Hockey Association of India, led by Bakshi with Harjinder as secretary general. The sports ministry does not recognise any national body of ice hockey as the administration of the sport has been mired in controversy in the recent past, with multiple factions claiming to be the official NSF. ALSO READ: IOA President PT Usha fails to get elected as SOM, will be ineligible to recontest for President https://sportstar.thehindu.com/other-sports/ioa-som-election-usha-result-releection-general-body-counting-votes-polled/article71682918.ece The IOA-appointed Electoral Officer Sanjay Kumar Srivastava rejected the objection by the IHAI faction led by Namgyal and accepted the nomination of Usha, which will allow her to vote as well as stand as a candidate for the IOA’s executive council polls on December 5. Against this decision, the Namgyal-led IHAI has filed a petition before the Delhi High Court. It has prayed for quashing the RO’s rejection order of its objections and holding the nominations (of Usha and Harjinder) to the electoral roll as “void and unlawful”. It has also prayed for directing the IOA to recognise its elections held on August 2 this year to be valid, thereby recognising it as the “lawful governing/Executive Committee”. Meanwhile, the Indian Golf Union (IGU), headed by Brijinder Singh, has also moved the Delhi High Court against the decision not to allow it to nominate two representatives to the IOA General Assembly. The matter will be heard on Thursday. The IGU was excluded from the list of 30 National Sports Federations eligible to vote in the IOA elections, issued by IOA-appointed Electoral Officer Srivastava on November 9. The IGU has two factions, one recognised by the IOA and the other by the Sports Ministry.

articles.title: New Zealand Tests could make or break India's WTC final hopes. Here's how - India Today
articles.summary: New Zealand Tests could make or break India's WTC final hopes. Here's how India Today
articles.content: India's hopes of reaching the World Test Championship (WTC) final could hinge on how they fare in their upcoming two-Test series against New Zealand. With only seven matches remaining in their 2025-27 campaign, the margin for error is shrinking, and a poor result against the Black Caps could leave them with a mountain to climb.India are currently fourth in the standings with 68 points and a points percentage (PCT) of 51.52. New Zealand lead the table with 72.22 per cent, followed by South Africa at 71.43 and Australia at 69.23. With only the top two teams qualifying for the 2027 final, India's next assignment assumes even greater significance.The numbers underline the importance of the series. Winning both Tests would lift India's PCT to 58.97, giving their campaign a much-needed boost. However, losing 0-2 would drag it down to 43.59 and leave them with an uphill task in their remaining five matches.The consequences of a 0-2 defeat would be severe. Even if India win all five remaining Tests against Australia at home next year, their PCT would rise only to 59.26. That might not be enough to secure a place in the final, potentially leaving them dependent on results elsewhere.Winning all seven remaining Tests, on the other hand, would take India to 70.37 per cent. Six victories would still lift them to 64.81 per cent, keeping them firmly in contention. However, two or more defeats could make their qualification prospects considerably tougher.WTC 2025-27 POINTS TABLENew Zealand: Matches – 6 | Won – 4 | Lost – 1 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 52 | PCT – 72.22%South Africa: Matches – 7 | Won – 5 | Lost – 2 | Drawn – 0 | Points – 60 | PCT – 71.43%Australia: Matches – 13 | Won – 9 | Lost – 4 | Drawn – 0 | Points – 108 | PCT – 69.23%India: Matches – 11 | Won – 5 | Lost – 4 | Drawn – 2 | Points – 68 | PCT – 51.52%Bangladesh: Matches – 8 | Won – 3 | Lost – 3 | Drawn – 2 | Points – 44 | PCT – 45.83%England: Matches – 16 | Won – 7 | Lost – 8 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 74 | PCT – 38.54%West Indies: Matches – 14 | Won – 3 | Lost – 8 | Drawn – 3 | Points – 46 | PCT – 27.38%Sri Lanka: Matches – 7 | Won – 1 | Lost – 2 | Drawn – 4 | Points – 13 | PCT – 15.48%Pakistan: Matches – 10 | Won – 2 | Lost – 7 | Drawn – 1 | Points – 4 | PCT – 3.33%AUSTRALIA, SOUTH AFRICA, NEW ZEALAND POSE BIGGEST THREATIndia's challenge is not limited to New Zealand. All three teams above them are serious contenders, and their current positions underline the scale of the task. New Zealand lead the standings with 72.22 per cent, followed by South Africa at 71.43 and Australia at 69.23.New Zealand have made an impressive start, winning four of their six Tests. However, their schedule remains demanding, with four Tests against Australia to follow the India series, before they take on Sri Lanka. South Africa, meanwhile, have seven matches remaining, including two against Bangladesh, three against England and two against Sri Lanka. Five wins from seven have already put the Proteas in a strong position.Australia have played the most Tests among the leading contenders, with 13 matches yielding nine victories. They have nine Tests left, including a four-Test series against New Zealand before travelling to India for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.India, therefore, cannot afford to leave their qualification hopes until their final assignment. A strong performance against New Zealand would not only improve their own position but also prevent the table-toppers from extending their advantage.INDIA'S REMAINING TESTS IN WTC 2023-25 CYCLENew Zealand tour (Away) – 2 Tests1st Test: November 19–23, 2026 – Wellington2nd Test: November 27–December 1, 2026 – ChristchurchAustralia tour of India (Home) – 5 Tests1st Test: January 21–25, 2027 – Nagpur2nd Test: January 29–February 2, 2027 – Chennai3rd Test: February 11–15, 2027 – Guwahati4th Test: February 19–23, 2027 – Ranchi5th Test: February 27–March 3, 2027 – Ahmedabad- Ends

articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 18: Punjab Hockey League Season 3 to get underway on Thursday Sportstar
articles.content: Chennai HOCKEY Punjab Hockey League Season 3 to kick off on November 19 The third season of the Punjab Hockey League (PHL), billed as the country’s biggest junior-level hockey tournament, begins on November 19 at the Olympian Balbir Singh Sr. International Hockey Stadium in Mohali. Indian internationals Manpreet Singh, Hardik Singh and Dilpreet Singh have been named Ambassadors. Organised by Roundglass and Hockey Punjab, the league has raised its prize money, the highest in Indian youth hockey, by 10 per cent from last season’s INR 30 lakh. Ten academy teams will play a league-cum-knockout format, with the league stage ending on December 3. articles.title: Sports Ministry forms 14-member committee to formulate ‘professionally managed’ leagues in India - The Hindu
articles.summary: Sports Ministry forms 14-member committee to formulate ‘professionally managed’ leagues in India The Hindu
articles.content: New Delhi The Sports Ministry on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) formed a 14-member committee to formulate a framework for developing “professionally managed, and financially sustainable” leagues in India with BCCI CEO and IPL COO Hemang Amin among the prominent members of the panel. The committee, which also includes IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer, has been mandated to assess existing ecosystem "constraints", and identify priority sports. It would be required to recommend measures to attract corporate capital, franchise ownership, sponsorships, broadcasting and digital rights, and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) financing. Empowered to consult National Sports Federations, existing league officials, investors, and sports technology firms, the committee has been given eight weeks to submit its final recommendations to the Ministry "While several sports leagues in the country have achieved varying levels of success, many disciplines with strong sporting and social potential face commercial viability hurdles during their initial stages," the ministry said in a statement. "Accordingly, the Committee will assess the present sports league ecosystem to identify the major issues and constraints affecting the establishment and sustainability of leagues...," it added. "...(the committee) will identify priority sports and categories, particularly Olympic sports, women's sports, youth sports, indigenous sports, and emerging sports, to recommend suitable operational models tailored to their sporting and commercial potential." The panel also includes top Sports Ministry officials Kunal, Joint Secretary (Governance), who will be its convener, and Vineel Krishna, Joint Secretary (Khelo India) along with representatives from major broadcasters like JioStar, Sony Network, Doordarshan, and Zee Network. The panel's formation is a major step towards Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya's stated goal of creating a robust league system in India. Currently, the leagues that have managed to capture the attention of the fans include IPL at the very top followed by franchise-based leagues in badminton, kabaddi, hockey and wrestling among others. However, almost all of them have battled financial issues with the hockey league facing the prospect of a shutdown within two years of its revival. The Ministry said a league ecosystem would not just help talent but would also bring in private investment and generate employment across sports management, broadcasting, technology, and events. "...the Committee will examine mechanisms for structured Government facilitation alongside active participation from the private sector, sports organisations, State Governments, local bodies, and communities. "This includes evaluating targeted interventions such as Viability Gap Funding (a one-time government grant to infrastructure projects), direct and indirect financial assistance, and concessional access to Government sports infrastructure," the Ministry stated. Additionally, the committee will propose strategies to integrate leagues with schools, colleges, universities, and local clubs to "foster grassroots participation". The composition of the Committee: Kunal, Joint Secretary (Governance) Convener, Vineel Krishna, (Joint Secretary -Khelo India), Raghuram Iyer (CEO, IOA, B Srinivasan (RIL), Hemang Amin (BCCI CEO and COO IPL), P.K.S.V. Sagar (GMR Sports), Sanjay Adesara (Adani Sportsline), Divyanshu Singh (JSW Sports), Ishan Chatterjee (Jio Hotstar), Rajesh Kaul (Sony Pictures), Anupam Swaroop (DD Sports), Parag Darade (Zee Entertainment), Abhijit Bhattacharya (BVL), Advocate Nandan Kamath.

articles.summary: Maharashtra declares four more talukas drought-hit; total rises to 308 The Hindu
articles.content: Mumbai Maharashtra government has declared four more talukas as drought affected areas, bringing the total to 308 out of 358 talukas. The four newly added talukas are Chiplun, Wada and Vikramgad in Konkan, and Dindori in Nashik district, whereas nine other talukas, including Hatkanangale,, Karveer and Gadhinglaj in Kolhapur district, and Pen and Mahad from Raigad are been assessed for the drought situation. Konkan region annually receives the highest rainfall. Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises Drought has devastated Maharashtra’s Beed district, pushing women farmers and labourers towards distress migration. Despite repeated pleas for employment, villagers say government job guarantees have failed them, even as the State announces a ₹6,728-crore package SPOTLIGHT Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises storyline 1 The announcement came on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), when Revenue Minister and chairman of the cabinet sub-committee on drought relief, Chandrashekhar Bawankule, said, “The four talukas were added after members at the meeting brought to notice the water scarcity and crop losses faced by farmers in these regions. 13 such proposals were made, four talukas were added to list.” The state government in October added 40 talukas to the first list of 265 talukas drought-hit, the total rose to 305. Trigger 1 and Trigger 2 have been applied in these talukas, making them eligible for assistance under the Centre’s National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) guidelines. The measures include a complete waiver of examination fees for students in drought-hit talukas, without any eligibility criteria. So far, ₹4,701.6 crore has been distributed to 94.3 lakh farmers across the State, as per the Agriculture Department. Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division received the highest assistance of ₹1,704.5 crore, then Nashik ₹1,001.2 crore and others.
